title: Microsoft Edge: Unsubscribe button on website notifications
summary: Pass: the roadmap facts, Group Policy paths and registry settings are supported, and searches found no documentation resolving the button-specific gaps. The cost rationale incorrectly attributes expected support effort to the roadmap, and one sentence overstates which policy pages describe the fallback behaviour.

claims.claim: Group Policy exposes the default notification control at Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge > Content settings > Default notification setting.
claims.quote: GP name: Default notification setting; GP path (Mandatory): Administrative Templates/Microsoft Edge/Content settings

claims.claim: Setting DefaultNotificationsSetting as REG_DWORD 2 under SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge selects the policy's block-notifications option.
claims.quote: BlockNotifications (2) = Don't allow any site to show desktop notifications; Path (Mandatory): SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge; Value name: DefaultNotificationsSetting; Value type: REG_DWORD

claims.claim: Group Policy exposes site notification blocking at Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge > Content settings > Block notifications on specific sites.
claims.quote: GP name: Block notifications on specific sites; GP path (Mandatory): Administrative Templates/Microsoft Edge/Content settings

claims.claim: Setting REG_SZ value 1 to https://www.contoso.com under SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge\NotificationsBlockedForUrls configures a blocked site.
claims.quote: Path (Mandatory): SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge\NotificationsBlockedForUrls; Value name: 1, 2, 3, ...; Value type: List of REG_SZ; SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge\NotificationsBlockedForUrls\1 = https://www.contoso.com

claims.claim: Setting REG_SZ value 1 to https://www.contoso.com under SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge\NotificationsAllowedForUrls configures an allowed site.

claims.claim: DefaultNotificationsSetting determines whether websites can display notifications by default.
claims.quote: Set whether websites can display desktop notifications. You can allow them by default ('AllowNotifications'), deny them by default ('BlockNotifications'), or have the user be asked each time a website wants to show a notification ('AskNotifications').

claims.claim: NotificationsBlockedForUrls takes URL patterns identifying sites that cannot display notifications, with a numbered registry value for each list entry.
claims.quote: Allows you to create a list of url patterns to specify sites that aren't allowed to display notifications. Value name: 1, 2, 3, ...; Value type: List of REG_SZ
